The opt-in concerns HomePod, but Apple's sentence says what is shared is phone call status 'from your device', i.e. this iPhone's data, and it is the only condition Apple attaches to that part of the nearby-device flow (E29/N05). Excluding it would leave the phone-call-status part of nearby_device_status wrongly recorded as having no switch. Apple gives no Settings path and does not say whether the opt-in is made on the iPhone (for example in the Home app) or on HomePod; settings_path is null for that reason. Grid effect: stops = the phone-call-status part of nearby_device_status (on opt-out); timers, alarms, shared media and proximity are not tied to it.
switches.apple_summary_claude_note: E29/E60: phone call status may be shared locally with nearby devices 'if you opted in to Personal Requests on HomePod'. This is a gate on the opted-in state; Apple does not say call status is not shared without the opt-in, and the action (local sharing with nearby devices) fits none of the six actions cleanly. No claim made; if the lead accepts gate-reading, the candidate would be nearby_device_status x siri_requests, stops on opt-out.

switches.name: Siri & Search (named on the Apple Store app page)
switches.settings_path: go to Settings > Siri & Search
switches.claude_note: Apple names a settings location, not a switch, so kind is 'settings_pane' (new kind; no existing kind fits). It concerns Siri Suggestions (Today at Apple session suggestions), so in_scope. 'Settings > Siri & Search' is probably the older name of the pane that ask-siri-dictation calls 'Settings > Siri', but Apple does not say so; record it as a wording issue (fifth way of naming the Siri settings root) and do not grid it, since no switch or effect is named. The ask-siri-dictation page has a parallel pane-level control ('see and control the full list of features that Siri personalizes ... by going to Settings > Siri') that is also not in switches.json; not on the checker's list, noted here only.
switches.apple_summary_claude_note: E62 'To change how Siri accesses your information, go to Settings > Siri & Search' is an instruction. E63 describes on-device Today at Apple suggestions with no off-state statement.

steps.text: go to Settings > Siri & Search

switches.name: Alerts & Shortcuts Automations (System Services)
switches.claude_note: Scope decision: adjacent. Apple describes 'an app or shortcut recommendation based on where you currently are', which resembles Siri Suggestions ('Siri can suggest shortcuts', E12), but this page never names Siri or Siri Suggestions, and says the iPhone 'will use' your location, not that it is sent to Apple. Tying it to siri_suggestions would be my inference, so it is not gridded as in_scope. settings_path is null because Apple gives only the generic instruction (System Services, then each service), not a path naming this service; the implied path is Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services > Alerts & Shortcuts Automations, and the on-device name should be checked.
